rules.sentence: UV rays are the primary risk factor for skin cancer development, making proper sun protection education crucial for immunocompromised individuals.
Actinic keratosis results from the proliferation of abnormal keratinocytes caused by UV radiation damage.
If left untreated, it carries the potential to progress to SCC.[9]
In immunosuppressed patients, this progression occurs more rapidly and with a lower likelihood of spontaneous regression.

Therefore, proactive management is essential, using liquid nitrogen cryotherapy for a limited number of lesions, or photodynamic therapy and topical treatments for more extensive lesions.[10]
Aggressive treatment of precancerous lesions is critical to preventing progression to invasive SCC.[11]

A systematic review found that liquid nitrogen cryotherapy as a standalone treatment achieves an average clearance rate of 72% at 1 to 3 months, 72% at 3 to 6 months, and 74% at 6 to 12 months, with improved efficacy when combined with 5-fluorouracil.

Photodynamic therapy yields optimal results when incorporated into multifaceted treatment approaches, showing the lowest recurrence rates when combined with an ablative fractional laser and trichloroacetic acid.
